206975307.description:
Hello! I'm Beau! I'm a very sweet boy with a unique feature. I'm a tripod! But don't let that fool you, I'm even more playful as ever! I love to go on walks and be outside. I even enjoy the water! I am house and kennel trained, and I love to hang out with the other dogs in my foster home. Sometimes we will play, but we all like to relax together too! While I get along with the dogs in my foster home, I do need slower intros with other dogs to help me feel comfortable. I am not a fan of hissing cats, so a home without cats would be best.

I enjoy puzzle toys and dog safe chews.  While I am a playful and adventerous boy, I also like to snuggle sometimes. Apartment life is too overwhelming for me, so I need a house, preferably with a fenced in yard, to call my forever home. However, the fenced in yard is not a dealbreaker since I enjoy going on walks.

I do have anxiety and allergies, so I take meds for them. But don't worry, I do really well taking them!

Are you my perfect match?

211913939.description:
Hi, I’m Pepper! 🐾

I’m an 8 ½ year-old bundle of love with the biggest heart and so much love to give! My foster family says I’m a special girl with a goofy personality, a playful spirit, and a heart that is truly one of a kind.

I may need a little extra patience and understanding when getting to know new people and navigating the world around me. New experiences and unfamiliar dogs can sometimes feel overwhelming, so I’m looking for someone who understands that building trust is a process. I may not open my heart overnight, but when I do, you’ll have a friend who loves with her whole heart. Once I trust you, you’ll get to see the real Pepper - the silly, affectionate, playful girl who loves to snuggle, give kisses, lean in for affection, and make you laugh. I have so much personality packed into this big body, and I truly believe I’m a lap dog! My favorite things include toys, treats, naps, and spending time with my people. And yes, my adorable snoring is just one of my many charms!

I currently live with another female dog, and we have a wonderful relationship. We love to play and chase each other, and she is a very special part of my world. While I do well with my resident dog, I have found that I’m most comfortable in a home where I don’t have to share my people or space with other dogs. I would likely thrive as the only dog in the home, where I can soak up all the love and attention. I’m looking for a quieter home with a patient, compassionate person or family who understands my needs and will give me the time and support I deserve. A female-led home would be a wonderful fit for me, and I would do best without children. I’m hoping for someone who sees the beauty in taking things slowly and understands that the most meaningful relationships are built one day at a time.

My foster family has watched me come so far. I’m learning that the world can be a wonderful place and that new experiences don’t always have to be scary. Every little bit of progress makes us so proud, and we know there is still so much happiness ahead of me. I’m a playful, loving girl who has so much more to discover. I may need someone willing to be patient, but I promise that the love I give in return is worth every moment. Once you become my person, you’ll have a loyal companion who wants nothing more than to be by your side. My foster family loves me dearly, and while saying goodbye will be incredibly difficult, they know there is someone out there who will see just how extraordinary I am.

I’m not looking for a perfect home. I’m looking for the right home - a home with patience, understanding, and a whole lot of heart. If you’re willing to give me the time I need to feel safe and loved, I’ll show you just how much love this big-hearted girl has to give ❤️

212359159.description:
Sweet Maple has been with us since she was 4-weeks-old. She came in with her mom (pictured with her) and 6 siblings, who have all be long since adopted. For some reason Maple sits and waits.

She started out going to the same events as her siblings, and got no interest. She was posted online everywhere, and got no interest.

We stopped attending events due to Maple being very shut down at them. We tried again once she was old enough to be on leash and outdoor events started; however, she was still very anxious and had a really hard time warming up to people.

Maple at home is an entirely different story. She warms up to people so fast, especially if you have treats, and a doggie friend for her to play with.

Maple is a very cautious girl, around people and will require another dog in the home for her to buddy up with.  She is great with all sizes of dogs, and she loves cats as well. She does very well with kids too!  She loves to be chased by them in the yard. Her favorite game is "chase me." She does okay on a leash, but would definitely do much better, and adjust so much easier, to a home with a fenced in yard.

At this point I could write a book about this sweet little devil, but I will wrap it but by saying she has some quirks and she will need to be on medication the rest of her life for urinary incontinence, but you won't find a better dog that can make you feel every emotion in one day, lol.

We truly love her and we know her perfect family will find her.

212449123.description:
Meet Jillian (a.k.a. Junie)!

If you are looking for a pup with a ton of personality and a lot of love, then Jillian is your girl.

With big amber eyes and a uniquely painted coat, Jillian is a little showstopper. She loves all humans she meets and is a huge sweetheart, but does need continued boundary work as she thinks the best way to let others know she is a fan is to get right up into their personal space! While she is smart and has picked up on cues and commands very quickly, ongoing training is still needed.

Jillian is now crate trained and has done well being crated for longer periods of time while her foster is at work. When crated, she tends to do better in a high-traffic area so she can observe what is going on around her and not miss out. The only time she cries anymore when crated is because she has a serious case of FOMO and just wants to join in the fun. While Jillian has not been left alone in the house outside the crate for long periods of time, during shorter bouts, she has done really well and usually just ends up lounging in the living room or sunroom.

Jillian is potty-trained and does very well with potty prompts once outside. She did clear our 3-foot fence at one point and had a nice little run in our neighbor’s yard so is currently on a lead even with a fenced-in backyard. As an almost 2-year-old, Jillian still has a lot of youthful energy and looks forward to going for her walk first thing in the morning. And while she has made a lot of progress over the last few months, Jillian does have a high prey drive and exhibits some excitable reactivity as a result.

Jillian is normally taken on a couple walks a day to work on her leash skills and she is catching on really quickly - we are learning to “leave it”, “wait”, and “eyes” (when needing her attention); she tends to crowd and pull on the leash so we are also working on side-by-side walking and pressure commands with the leash. She also still struggles with off-leash recall but with continued patience and consistency, will no doubt continue to improve. Overall, she would greatly benefit from working with a trainer as it appears that most things are still very new to her.

While Jillian initially did well with the resident dog, more recently, she seems to be struggling to read different social cues and has shown some aggressive reactivity. As a result, we have been keeping her on a lead or in the crate as a precaution when both dogs are in a shared space in the house. Since Jillian was found as a stray, it is hard to know her history with other dogs; she does express high interest in playing with other dogs but will require high levels of monitoring.

In just a short amount of time, Jillian has learned both the verbal and nonverbal signals for “sit”, “wait”, “hands in”, “stay” and “lie down”. She transports well and loves her weekly outdoor adventures at Fort Snelling. Overall, Jillian's ideal home is with an active family or person who is patient, does not have any other pets, is in a house (she does have a heavy bark!) with a high fenced-in yard. If you are ready for a lively spirit, funny personality, and unconditional companionship - look no further than Jillian!

Meet Buttercup!

Buttercup is a sweet, gentle pup who can be a little shy and reserved when meeting new people, but once she feels safe she becomes very loving and loyal to her people.

Buttercup has low-to-moderate energy and enjoys both playtime and cuddles. She loves playing fetch and will happily bring the ball back so you can throw it again. She’s also extremely treat and food motivated, which makes training fun and rewarding. Belly rubs, snacks, and greeting her people when they come home are some of her favorite things.

She is good with other dogs, but can be reactive when she sees them from a distance and does best with slow introductions. Buttercup doesn’t need another dog in the home, but a calm, friendly dog could help build her confidence.

Buttercup is afraid of men and will need a patient home that allows her time to warm up. Because she isn’t familiar with toddlers, she would do best with older children. She sleeps well in her crate at night and learned potty training quickly.

Buttercup cannot live with cats.

She’s a very sweet, cuddly girl who has clearly had a difficult past and just needs a patient family who will give her the love and security she deserves.

Hi, I'm Norman! My foster mom scooped me up when she heard how I came in to rescue.. I was hanging around the hospital, trying to find some food, when some big dogs came at me and chased me away. Luckily a nice lady who worked there came to help me. I've adjusted to the good life in my foster home really well. There are three other pups here, which I absolutely LOVE! I am learning a lot from the older ones, and I just love to play with the other puppy. My foster mom says my play style is somewhat rough, but I prefer to call it exuberant.

I'm an energetic guy who is always up for an adventure! I am very food motivated and happy to have any snack - even the healthy ones! I eat and sleep in my crate, and occasionally my foster mom will find my hanging out in there by choice! My foster mom tells me her favorite thing about me is my ears, because they are a good mix of floppy and standing up. If you think we might be a good fit, apply to meet me! My foster mom would be happy to tell you all about me!

From my foster mom: Chat GPT estimates that he will be around 50 lbs fully grown, so if you are looking for a pup with the looks of a big dog, but on the smaller side, Norman is for you! I think he would do best in a home with another dog! Both for his happiness, and to allow him to burn some of his boundless energy off easily. He has lived with small children before, and his energy level and love for play chomping did not work out well. He is very sweet and gentle with children when meeting them, but it may be best for him to go to a home with older children only. I am hoping he grows out of some of that, but only time will tell! Norman is a great dog and will be perfect for someone who is very active. When he finally settles down he is a great snuggler!

Shalla is an old soul with a youthful heart. There’s a gentle wisdom about her that’s apparent the moment you see her—but step closer, and she’ll happily surprise you with joyful hops and rapid‑fire kisses. She’s the kind of dog who reminds you that some hearts stay forever young.

Shalla has spent much of her life being a devoted mama, and now it’s her turn to be cared for. And care for her you will—because she is stunning. From her beautifully lined eyes to her glowing golden coat, she turns heads wherever she goes.

We aren’t quite sure of her breed, but she has the majestic face of a wolf paired with big, elegant paws—though she’s not especially tall. Her coat is thick, sleek, and surprisingly easy to maintain considering how full it is.

Shalla would thrive in a home with people around most of the time. She loves kids and enjoys being part of the action. She’s polite with other dogs—she likes them well enough but doesn’t necessarily need a canine companion to be happy. What she does need is togetherness. Shalla doesn’t love being alone, and adopters should be prepared to use a heavy‑duty crate and possibly medication when away from home.

Aside from that, she is an amazing, well‑behaved dog who simply wants to be close to her people. And yes—we know you’re wondering—she has had zero accidents.

If you’re looking for a loyal, affectionate companion who will soak up every moment by your side, Shalla is ready to finally be someone’s “baby.”

213593830.description:
Meet Mariska! ❤️

Mariska has been through more than most dogs ever should, but every day she's learning that people can be kind, love can be permanent, and home is a safe place. In 2025, we rescued a litter of her puppies, but we were finally able to rescue her this year. After spending so much of her life surviving and raising babies, this sweet mama is ready to retire, relax, and let someone take care of her for a change.

She's embracing indoor life and making incredible progress. Mariska has discovered the joy of toys and is wonderfully goofy when she plays—leaping, hopping, tossing toys into the air, and catching them herself. She's also incredibly smart! She already knows how to ring the bells to go outside, kennel on cue, sit, leave it, and she's eager to keep learning.

Once Mariska trusts you, she becomes the sweetest little shadow, happily following her favorite person from room to room. A few tasty treats, gentle face scratches, and belly rubs are the fastest way to win her heart. At the end of the day, she's happiest curled up beside you, handing out cuddles and plenty of kisses.

Mariska also enjoys the company of other dogs. She has become friends with every foster dog she's met, but she needs slow, thoughtful introductions and usually takes a day or two to feel comfortable. Because of this, she'd do best in a home that won't expect her to enjoy busy dog parks or daycare settings.

Due to her past, Mariska needs a patient adopter who understands that trust takes time. New people can still be frightening for her, and if she's approached too quickly, she may react out of fear. Her foster family is helping her build confidence, but she'll need someone committed to continuing that journey. For now, she would do best in a home without young children.

When Mariska first entered rescue, she struggled with separation anxiety, barking in her kennel, pawing at the door, or pulling nearby items inside for comfort. She has made tremendous progress, though it's possible some of those behaviors may temporarily return as she adjusts to a new home.

Mariska is looking for someone who will see past her fears and appreciate the incredible dog she's becoming. If you're willing to give her patience, consistency, and unconditional love, she'll reward you with unwavering loyalty, endless affection, and the joy of watching a once-forgotten dog truly blossom into the companion she was always meant to be. ❤️

After spending years taking care of everyone else, it's finally Carlotta's turn to be loved. She's ready for a family who will cherish her, appreciate her loyal heart, laugh at her adorable sideways ear, and give her the forever home she's been waiting for.

Could Carlotta be the missing piece of your family?

pads like a pro. The only time I have an accident is when I get super tired.

favorite part of school is getting the treats!

I absolutely love other dogs and I love kids! My perfect forever home will have plenty of outdoor

playtime, some fun furry or human siblings, and a family who appreciates a brave girl with a lot of look-at-me attitude.

Because of this, we think she would thrive in a home with another dog so she has someone to play with and someone to show her the ropes. He came to us with some skin issues and a very thin coat, but he’s receiving care and with some TLC, good nutrition, and time, he’ll have the best glow up. Soon he’ll be sporting a beautiful, thick winter coat again. We’re working on helping him put on some much-needed weight as well.

He may have had a rough start, but this boy has so much love to give. He’s gentle, eager to please, and just seems incredibly grateful to be with people who care about him.

He’s ready for the next chapter with a lot of love to give and we can’t wait to see the happy, healthy, confident dog he becomes.

214265511.description:
Tito is suspected to have come to us from a hoarding situation after potentially being bred / a "stud." After a difficult start to life, he is understandably guarded and defensive, and he will need a patient, understanding adopter who is willing to let him build trust at his own pace.

Tito is smart, sassy, independent, and incredibly curious. He’s a bit like a “wisp of smoke”—quick, elusive, and determined to keep all four paws on the ground! He isn’t comfortable being picked up yet, but we’re making progress every day.

He has especially begun to trust his foster mom, choosing to curl up beside her in her recliner. Because of this, we suspect Tito may be more comfortable with women and may need extra time to feel safe around men. He is also gradually warming up to his teenage foster grandsons, showing us that his circle of trust can grow with patience and consistency.

Tito appears to have had little-to-no training before coming into rescue. He is currently pee-pad trained and sleeps quite a bit.

For now, Tito is not a fan of other dogs. He reacts strongly toward the resident dog, so they are kept separated. He is also a significant flight risk and has managed to escape harnesses and take off, so his adopter will need to be extremely careful and use secure, escape-proof equipment and management.

Tito is not going to be an “easy” dog, but he is a worthwhile one. His adopter will need to be committed to giving him time, structure, patience, and plenty of opportunities to learn that the world can be a safe place. In return, they’ll get a smart, savvy, energetic little companion.

Tito is looking for someone who understands that trust isn't given overnight—it’s earned one tiny step at a time. And with Tito, those tiny steps are incredibly rewarding.

213961460.description:
Meet Puck! ❤️

If you’re looking for a loyal cuddle buddy, a gentle soul, and a dog who would happily be your copilot on every adventure, Puck might just be your perfect match!

Puck is an incredibly easy companion to welcome into your home. This sweet, affectionate boy is happiest when he’s close to his people, soaking up all the love he can get and giving plenty of kisses in return. While he’s quiet and well-behaved in his kennel, his favorite place is much closer to his humans—preferably curled up beside you on the couch, enjoying some serious cuddle time.

Puck has the most irresistibly big, fluffy, squishy face, and he absolutely LOVES having his cheeks rubbed. ❤️

His foster family has been pleasantly surprised by Puck’s lower energy level, especially considering his breed mix. An Embark DNA test revealed that Puck is an Australian Cattle Dog, Siberian Husky, and German Shepherd mix. Despite those active breeds, Puck isn’t currently interested in running around or playing with the other dogs in his foster home. Instead, you’ll usually find him happily lying near his humans, soaking up their company. He hasn’t shown much interest in toys either, although that may change as he continues to heal, settle in, and gain confidence in his new home.

He is currently living in a foster home with cats. His breed tends to have a higher prey drive and he has shown that, so he would do best in a home without cats.

Puck is still discovering the joys of food and treats and is gradually becoming more food- and bone-motivated. He already knows how to sit and is eager to learn more, especially when it means spending time with his favorite people. Like many happy dogs, he may occasionally jump up when he’s excited to see you, but it’s all out of love.

Puck also recently underwent TPLO surgery in July and is recovering incredibly well! He’s already walking on all four legs almost like nothing ever happened. Once he is fully recovered, he’ll be ready to enjoy all the walks, car rides, adventures, couch cuddles, and quality time his heart desires.

Puck may not be the dog who needs constant action or endless games of fetch. He may be the dog who simply wants to be near you—following you around the house, curling up beside you, riding along in the car, enjoying a good sniff on a walk, and reminding you just how wonderful it is to have a loyal friend by your side.

If you’re looking for a sweet, affectionate companion who will happily trade endless kisses, cuddles, and car rides, then Puck is ready to meet you. ❤️🐾

He needs reinforcement and reminds he is part of the family. his first response is to isolate in his kennel, but just calling him back to you reminds him he is wanted and he thrives on it. he loves having his kennel door open just in case he needs a min to himself... he is going to add such love and joy to whatever family he goes to... he just needs to be loved up the rest of his life. I'm Sarge! I have so much love to give, and absolutely nothing is stopping me from finding my family. After getting injured in an accident, the lovely team at Rescue Network came out to save me, but I couldn't leave my pack behind. With an injured leg, I went to find my furry friends. I forgot to tell my rescuers though. I gave them quite the scare when they could not find me. One month later, I appeared again. This time with my friends, ready to be rescued too!

I lost a leg from the accident. Don't be sad, because I'm not letting that stop me one bit. I'm recovering and adjusting beautifully. I've had a taste of the indoor life, and I can't get enough. I especially love cuddling in a cozy spot and laying my head on my people's lap. I'm doing amazing with kennel and potty training. I'll learn whatever I need to, as long as it means I get to be by your side.

214490496.description:
Nos is a timid young adult who is learning to trust people. He takes a bit of time to warm up, but once he has accepted you, he will follow you everywhere. He has attached himself to our 18-year-old son and is thrilled to hang out and snuggle with him.

Once he’s comfortable with you, Nos soaks up the scratches and attention. He loves to nap on the couch, with his head in your lap. He’s even offered a few tentative kisses in the 24 hours we’ve had him.

Nos is just beginning to decompress and gain confidence in life and his environment. He needs people to be slow and patient with him for now. He doesn’t like to feel like he’s being chased or forced to do something - he’d rather think things are his idea. He will go in a crate and hang out a bit, but will bark if you leave him there. He’s happy to explore in our fenced backyard, but it works best if we open the door and let him head out when he’s ready. This will improve in time; he’s had a lot to figure out in a short amount of time.

He’s not yet interested in playing with the other dogs at our house - because they’re not the dogs he’s used to. But he’s been relatively patient with meeting them.

When Nos meets people, he’s more comfortable when they get down to his level (or sit on a couch), rather than tower over him. He will take a slow sniff, then allow you to pet him. After all, he knows he is darling!

Nos is a beautiful boy! He’s got the sweetest chocolate eyes and super soft fur. With time and patience, he will make a great pet!

214440721.description:
Meet Flik, a natural-born leader who loves bossing her siblings around! She’s smart, curious, and adventurous. This medium-energy girl loves to explore and is highly food motivated, making her a great candidate for training.

Flik is doing wonderfully with potty training, sleeping 6–8 hours in her crate overnight without accidents and immediately going outside when she wakes up. She loves to play with dogs, although her foster’s older dogs aren’t quite as enthusiastic about her puppy energy.

Like any puppy, Flik is a serious chewer, so plenty of appropriate chew toys and puppy-proofing will be essential. She enjoys fluffy and tug toys and would likely love some sturdy chews, too!

Flik hasn’t been tested with cats or children tested yet. She’s a confident, curious little girl with a big personality, and she’s ready for a family who will keep her busy, continue her training, and give her plenty of adventures!

214441231.description:
Mojave is the friendliest foster we have ever had.

New person? You’re his new favorite person instantly.

New dog? He’s super curious and wants to play immediately. But he can also be redirected away from a nervous dog with a treat.

Want to snuggle? Sit down in a recliner or on a couch and he’ll be right over, looking for some scratches in return.

Want to teach him a new trick? Have some treats on hand. He’s super food motivated.

Need to leave him home alone? Mojave does well in a crate with a stuffed Kong (even at night.) Just a little whimpering, then he settles right in. But he also does well free roaming a contained space for a few hours.

Want a snuggle bug in bed? He’d love the invite!

Looking for an office mate? Mojave is happy to hang out, and might even try to sneak into your lap as you work.

Live in an apartment? He’s a good apartment size and rarely barks. (Mostly when he wants to play or wants attention, but even then it’s brief and not very loud.)

This is truly one delightful little guy who would do well in so many different households! He views every new person, dog and experience as an opportunity for fun! (We were told when we picked him up that he may not be good with cats, but we haven’t been able to test that.) He’s super flexible, loves everybody and is one of the nicest dogs around!

214344991.description:
Lorraine is a beautiful, fun loving youngster who remains fearful of unfamiliar sounds, and sudden movements. She can be a rascal when she feels comfortable and confident as far as checking out what’s on the kitchen counter that may be tasty.

She walks well on a leash as long as her person is alert for squirrels!!

She loves to sit patiently and watch out the window for squirrels. She is not a barker even with those hound dog ears.

Lorraine would do best with another dog in the family to help her feel safe and show her the ropes, and she would benefit from having a fenced in backyard. She enjoys playing chase with any dog willing to run fast, and she likes to wrestle (very quietly) with the foster family’s cattle dog.

She’s not been around cats or young kids.  Pretty sure she would appreciate the more predictable movements of adolescents.

Lorraine can be quite willful when it comes to going in her crate, or putting on her collar to go for a walk. She’s very food motivated so she would thrive in a beginning level obedience class.

She’s a beautiful dog looking for someone who works from home so she doesn’t have to spend a great deal of time in her crate. She sleeps quietly on her own bed next to her foster parents.

Lorraine has faced a truckload of traumas and daunting challenges in her short life. She’s waiting for the right person or family to envelope her with care, structure, and love to help her become her best self. She’s soooo worth the investment of time and energy!

214441275.description:
Tennessee is a sweet, affectionate young pup who is so happy to have a safe place to call home. She has a medium energy level with bursts of puppy enthusiasm and loves playing with toys, spending time with her people, and hanging out with her dog friends. She’s intelligent, eager to learn, and has already shown that she can listen when redirected.

Tennessee is doing well with house training and is currently going potty outside about 90% of the time. Puppy pads by the door help her when she doesn’t quite make it outside. Like many young dogs, she is still working on her manners and can be mouthy and energetic, but she responds well to a firm “no” and will benefit from continued positive training and consistency.

She gets along well with other dogs and would likely love having a young, playful canine companion to help keep her company and burn off some of that puppy energy. The rare time she barks is to try to encourage the older dogs to play with her. She currently sleeps peacefully on a dog bed alongside her foster dog siblings all night.

Tennessee is interested in cats and wants to play with them a little more enthusiastically than they would prefer! With her young age and trainability, she may be able to learn appropriate manners around cats, but a home with dog-savvy cats and a family committed to supervision and training would be best. She has not been tested with young children, so that would be something to consider carefully.

She is also a mouser! She is smart and very alert and has caught a vole and a mouse in the yard.

She is still learning that meals are going to keep coming, and she tends to gobble her food as though she might not get another chance. Slow feeding and consistency should help her learn that she is safe and cared for.

Tennessee doesn’t seem to be a flight risk and appears incredibly grateful to have a home and people who care for her. She’s a young dog with plenty to learn, but underneath that puppy energy is a loving, intelligent girl who is going to make someone an absolutely wonderful companion.

Tennessee would thrive with a family who is ready to give her the structure, training, patience, and love she needs to become her very best self.

She plays gently and accepts love from adults (male and female) as well as our 18-month-old toddler. She still mouths (hands and ankles) periodically as puppies do but only towards adults and tends to only do so when over tired. Tansy plays wonderfully with our 11-month-old husky and holds her ground even though he is larger and a bit of a bulldozer. Her calm and curious presence turns into zoomies when playing and she loves running around in the yard with our husky or playing tug with thier toys. She also enjoys walks on leash but be prepared for her to sniff ALL the things! Tansy is a loveable and sweet puppy that enjoys playing and exploring as much as cuddles with her people. Little but mighty, Tansy has everything to offer to her new family.

214354283.description:
Looking for a spunky, energetic kitten?! Cari is your girl!

When she first arrived, she was pretty sick, but after a quick visit to the vet and the necessary meds, Cari was feeling better almost immediately! It wasn't long before her brave, energetic personality really began to shine! You may notice her right eye looks a little different. This is a temporary effect of the severe upper respiratory infection she had when she arrived in our care, but it should resolve on its own now that Cari has finished her meds and is feeling like a healthy kitten again!

Cari is a very playful and social girl. She loves being around people and even better if they are up for a play session! She is obsessed with her crinkle ball, but can make a toy out of literally anything... whether you like it or not :) This includes fingers and toes... but we are working on redirecting her with actual toys when that happens! For this reason, older children may be a better fit for her. She has even found dog toys to be equally as fun as cat toys! Cari has been living with 3 dogs and 3 cats. She LOVES to play with one of our foster dogs. They have become really great friends! She even likes to nap near him. So safe to say she is dog friendly! She has been very hesitant about meeting the resident cats, but with time and proper introductions, I think she could do well with a friendly, playful feline companion.

Cari plays to her heart's content, which also means she works up quite an appetite! Cari is a huge fan of meal time and doesn't appear to be picky! She loves it all! So no fighting with this one when it comes to choosing what's for dinner. That's a huge win in our book! She also does really well with being picked up and carried. And when she wants to be put down, she will certainly let you know with her  big girl meow! Once and awhile, mainly at bedtime, she will curl up and snuggle with us humans for a little bit which is a real treat.

Cari is the perfect mix of sweet & spunky- and will certainly keep you laughing every day with her crazy, playful antics!

214347367.description:
Meet the Salad Litter!

These tiny pups are hard at work mastering their most important jobs: napping, eating, playing, and learning how to be dogs! They’re soft, clumsy little bundles of joy who are already stealing hearts wherever they go.

Their mama, Ambrosia, looks like a German Shepherd, and based on some of the pups’ features, there’s likely a little Husky mixed in too!

The Salad pups love piling on top of each other for meals, playtime, and naps. They’re discovering the joy of chewing on puppy toys, soaking up cuddles from their humans, and giving the sweetest puppy-breath kisses.

These little ones are looking for adopters who understand that puppies take patience, consistency, and lots of love. Their new families should be ready for potty training, teething, basic obedience, and all the adorable chaos that comes with learning how to be a puppy!

Because socialization and potty-training routines are so important at this age, they’ll need homes where they won’t be left alone for long periods of time.

If you’re ready to add one of these sweet salad sprouts to your family, apply to adopt today! Before you know it, one of these little pups could be snuggled right in your arms.

214490493.description:
Meet Fresca! Sweet, shy, and slowly discovering just how wonderful life can be, Fresca is ready to find a family of her very own!

Fresca came into rescue after raising a litter of puppies, and now it’s finally her turn to be the baby! She can be a little nervous and unsure when she first meets people or enters a new environment, but once she realizes she’s safe, her personality starts to shine. Give her a little time, patience, and some gentle encouragement, and you’ll see her come out of her shell more and more each day.

One of Fresca’s favorite recent discoveries? Playing with her foster dog sibling! She has really started to loosen up and enjoys romping and having fun with her resident dog. A friendly, patient dog in her forever home could be a wonderful companion for her, but is not required.

Fresca is also a pretty quiet girl. She doesn't bark when someone comes to the door, which is a nice bonus! Every now and then, though, she likes to remind everyone that she has a voice by letting out a dramatic little howl—usually when she’s unhappy about something. Think of it as her way of filing a formal complaint.

She's making great progress with potty training! While we wouldn't call her fully potty trained just yet, she's had very few accidents since her first couple of days in foster care and is catching on beautifully. She also enjoys her kennel and sleeps there peacefully at night. We're still working on getting her to go into her kennel on command, but she's making progress.

And don't let her shy personality fool you—once Fresca trusts you, she is incredibly affectionate. She loves being close to her people and has a very sweet, loving side that comes out once she feels comfortable.

She's also a surprisingly good little walking buddy! Fresca walks nicely on a leash and doesn't really pull, making her a pleasure to take along on adventures.

Fresca's ideal family will understand that she may need a little time to adjust and won't expect her to become their best friend on day one. Her ideal home will be a calmer home with older kids. She needs people who are willing to give her patience, reassurance, and time to trust.  In return, you'll get to watch an incredibly rewarding transformation as this once-scared mama discovers confidence, playfulness, and the joy of being someone's beloved dog.

Fresca has spent her time taking care of everyone else. Now she's ready for someone to take care of her.

Fresca at a glance:

•	Former mama who is ready to be someone's baby

•	Shy at first, but very affectionate once she trusts you

•	Enjoys playing with other dogs

•	Quiet overall; doesn't bark at the door

•	Occasionally howls when she's displeased

•	Making excellent progress with potty training

•	Sleeps happily in her kennel at night

•	Walks surprisingly well on leash with very little pulling

•	Needs a patient family willing to give her time to settle in

•	Coming out of her shell more every day!

If you're looking for a gentle girl whose trust will feel like something truly special to earn, Fresca might just be your girl.

Joel is affectionate, attentive and picks up on new tricks quickly. He gets the occassional burst of energy and loves taking walks. He would be a great dog to take on adventures! He also settles well, doesn't bark much and sleeps great in his kennel at night.  While he gets excited for treats, he is not overly motivated by food and shows no signs of resource guarding.

Joel gets along great with the 10-year-old human who lives in his foster home,  and is always happy to see her. The dog in his foster home is not as excited as Joel is to play, so they haven't spent a ton of time together. I think Joel would be fine as a solo pet or with another dog in the home who matches his energy and enjoys playing. He seems to have a stronger prey drive, so living with a cat may be difficult. Joel exhibits some classic German Shepherd traits too, including the occasional land shark behavior, so experience with that breed would be helpful.

If you are looking for a best buddy to explore with, Joel could be the perfect dog for you!

Despite everything she has been through in her short life, LaCroix is an incredibly sweet, loving soul with so much affection left to give. From day one, she has been a protective, devoted mother who gently trusted her foster family with her babies.

Once she settled into her foster home, LaCroix revealed her true self: a total cuddle bug and a loyal little shadow who wants to be wherever her favorite human is. She is working hard on her house training and is doing fantastic with a regular routine.

LaCroix has recently learned how to do zoomies, and has picked out one special toy, her "emotional support sashimi" that she loves to hop on after you squeak it.

LaCroix has handled a busy foster home like a champ, but after everything she's survived, she truly deserves to be someone’s prized companion and spoiled pet (or placed in a calm, quieter environment). She will need slow, patient introductions to new animals, but in return, she will give you endless love, loyalty, and snuggles.

About the Family:

These sweet puppies and their mom were brought into rescue after an emergency surrender situation where they urgently needed a safe landing. When they first arrived, Mama LaCroix and her four boys were dangerously underweight—the pups were small enough to fit in the palm of a hand, and Mama was skin and bones.

After just a few days of consistent food, clean water, safety, and love, their true personalities blossomed! Today, Mama is weaning off her babies and putting on weight, and is looking for her furever home.

214347362.description:
Mama Ambrosia is the proud mom of the adorable “Salad Mix” puppies, and her foster family has lovingly called her “Mom". After spending her time raising, loving, and protecting her  nine babies, this sweet girl is finally ready for something she’s never truly had: a forever family of her very own.

Ambrosia is a loving, loyal girl with a big personality and an even bigger heart. She absolutely loves carrying around her favorite toys and soaking up affection. She’s also incredibly smart! In just the few short weeks she’s been in rescue, she has already learned sit, drop it, outside, and shake. She’s eager to learn and continues to make amazing progress every day.

Like any good mama, Ambrosia can be very protective of what she considers valuable. She has some food reactivity and can occasionally become barrier-aggressive when she has food or high-value treats. She has come a long way in just a few weeks, though, and her progress has been wonderful to watch. When she first arrived, she also showed some toy guarding, but she has not demonstrated that behavior recently.

Ambrosia likely could do well with respectful children given her sweet and affectionate personality, but she has not yet been formally tested with kids, so any introductions would need to be thoughtful and supervised.

After giving her puppies the love, protection, and guidance they needed, she deserves the chance to be someone's baby now. She’s ready for a family who will continue to help her grow, celebrate her progress, and show her just how wonderful life can be.

If you're looking for a loyal companion, a smart girl with plenty of personality, and a best friend who has a whole lot of love left to give, Ambrosia is ready to meet you.

INTRODUCING YUKI! This sweet girl is looking for a family, and is hoping it is you!

Yuki is a gentle, good-natured and smart girl. She is potty trained. In her previous home she learned to ring a bell when she wanted to go outside. She is kennel trained, but definitely prefers to be right by your side. She is the best friend you always wanted.

Yuki can be skittish in a new environment, therefore she would love a patient family that will allow her to get comfortable at her own pace. A calm and predictable home with kids 12 and up would be best for her. Chaos can be to overwhelming to her.

Her ideal home would include the following:

Walking and squeaky tennis balls are an absolute must! She is an enthusiastic walker! She pulls a bit to begin with. She wants to get all the smells in, but she will settle down after a short time. Chasing and squeaking her tennis ball is a favorite pastime.

A fenced yard to chase that ball and show off her zoomies.

Yuki really enjoys chasing the cats. While she hasn’t been allowed to get very close to them, living with cats may not be a successful fit.

Calmer dogs only. Yuki does not enjoy dogs that get in her face. If there is another dog in your home, it would need to be a more laid-back pup. She will need a slow, safe introduction to her new sibling.

A window to observe the outside world. She likes to lay in the sun and see the goings on in the neighborhood.

Though she has her playful and adventurous side, sitting beside you on the couch is her favorite way to wrap up the day. If you are a looking for the ultimate companion Yuki is your girl. She is excited to meet you!

Starbies loves the freedom of being outdoors and would happily join you on your adventures, but she is just as content to curl up and lounge quietly when it’s time to relax. Now that her puppies are taken care of, it’s Mama Starbies’ turn to find the loving home she deserves—a person or family who will show her what being loved truly feels like.

214581232.description:
Quarter is truly a gem, a calm and incredibly friendly pup who's just beginning to discover the joys of being part of a loving home. He’s got such a gentle soul and is proving to be a real sweetheart with everyone he meets.

When it comes to playtime, he's a happy participant, especially with our other dog. He enjoys a good romp, but he's not one to bounce off the walls all day – I'd say he has a lovely medium energy level, happy to play but equally content to curl up for a nap. He gets along beautifully with other dogs, respecting their space and inviting them to play in a calm manner.

We have a cat, and Quarter is quite the respectful roommate! She can rub right up against him or zoom past, and he just offers a mild glance of curiosity. He certainly isn't bothered by her presence, making him a great candidate for a multi-pet household.

One of his most endearing qualities is how wonderful he is with children. Our grandchildren adore him, and he loves to simply be near them, whether it's lounging on the floor or snuggling on the sofa. We've quickly learned that he has an incredibly tolerant nature – you can easily take things from his mouth, and even little hands getting close to his face doesn't faze him in the slightest. There’s never a growl or a snap; he's just pure patience and sweetness.

He's making fantastic progress with his kennel training. He sleeps soundly in it all night and feels perfectly comfortable settling in there when we need to leave the house. After a couple of minor mishaps right at the start, he's been spotless ever since, showing he really understands it's his safe, clean space.

Potty training is still a work in progress, but he's definitely getting the hang of it! While he might occasionally have an accident indoors, they are almost always right by the door, which tells us he’s trying his very best to communicate when it's time to go outside. With a little more consistency, he’ll have it down pat.

Leash walks are an adventure for Quarter! He walks pretty well on a leash, though I wouldn't say it's his favorite activity just yet – he’s still exploring the big wide world one sniff at a time. We're also working on basic commands like "sit," and he's quite clever, especially when his canine companion isn't around to distract him with fun.

All in all, Quarter is a curious, calm, friendly, and incredibly cuddly boy who is just soaking up all the love and learning what it means to be a cherished member of a family. He’s going to bring so much joy to his future home!

If you're looking for a happy, playful companion with a big smile and an even bigger love for fetch, Fisher may be your guy!

Fisher is a fun-loving young adult who is ball driven and absolutely thrilled to retrieve. Toss a ball his way and you've made his day! He also loves squeaky toys, a good bone, and pretty much anything that gives him a chance to play.

But don't let his playful side fool you—Fisher knows how to relax, too. After a good walk and some time to get his energy out, he's more than happy to curl up on the couch beside his person for some quality cuddle time. His signature happy smile is sure to brighten your day.

As a young adult, Fisher is naturally curious about the world around him. He likes to pull on walks, squirrels and leaves blowing in the wind can be pretty exciting and may tempt him to give chase! Like any young dog, he'd benefit from continued training and reminders about staying off things he's curious about. The good news is that Fisher has a good recall, especially when his person gives him a firm "no" or redirects him.

Fisher would love a home with a backyard where he can run, play fetch, and enjoy being a dog. Even better? A playmate who enjoys having fun as much as he does!

Cats are currently unknown, so slow introductions and appropriate supervision would be recommended.

Fisher's Favorites:

- Chasing and retrieving balls

- Squeaky toys

- A good bone

- Walks and adventures

- Making everyone smile

- Couch cuddles after playtime

Fisher is looking for someone who will enjoy his playful young-adult energy, continue helping him learn, and appreciate all the love and happiness he has to give.

If you're looking for a goofy, happy, ball-loving boy who can go from "LET'S PLAY!" to "come cuddle with me" in no time, Fisher is ready to meet you!

214663441.description:
Hello, my name is Sadie. I’m a kind, gentle soul that was just rescued from the outside life.

I am SO happy about my new start in life. I’m always smiling and wagging my tail.  I have a very mellow demeanor and I’m very quiet. I am kennel trained and really love my bed in there.

I love kids they give me lots of belly rubs. Any love, I’ll take it!

I’m still new and resting, so I haven’t met any other pets yet. But I lived outside with many dogs and did very well so my foster mom is confident I’ll love other doggy friends.

I haven’t met any kitties, but my gentle demeanor should do fine with anything smaller than me.

I’m over all a sweet angel baby.

I will make a great companion for a family and I’m so excited for this opportunity of being loved. I can’t wait to find a family of my own!

214580940.description:
Meet Chloe your new favorite snuggle buddy!

This sweet girl is an absolute lovebug who wants nothing more than to be close to her people. Whether she’s curled up on your lap, snuggled beside you, or simply following you around the house, she is happiest when she’s near you.

She is fully potty trained and has been incredibly quiet. In the week I’ve known her, I haven’t heard her bark once! She loves playing with her toys, but cuddling with her humans may be her favorite activity of all.

She’s still working on her leash skills and learning how to be a better walking companion. While we don’t yet know how she would do living with other dogs or cats, she has done well meeting other dogs while out on walks.

If you’re looking for a gentle, affectionate sweetheart who will happily be your little shadow and professional cuddle partner, she may be your girl.

214628324.description:
Hi! I’m a goofy, sweet, curious little guy who is having the BEST time learning how wonderful life can be with a family!

I absolutely adore my 8- and 9-year-old human foster sisters and somehow always know when they’ve left the room - I have to go find them and see what they’re up to! I also love playing with my 10-year-old husky foster sister, who has been a wonderful role model as I learn all my good-boy skills.

I’m smart, loving, and playful, but I also know how to settle in for a nap or a serious snuggle session. I love toys, I’m doing great with my potty training, and I’m happiest when I’m with my people. I really like my crate at nighttime and bark to let my foster mom know it's time to get in and get cozy!

I’m still a puppy, so I have plenty to learn, but I’m off to a fantastic start. All I need now is a forever family who will keep teaching me, playing with me, and loving me as much as I’ll love them.

(Skunk is recovering from non-contagious mange and receives weekly bath treatments. His coat will grow back in no time!).

He’s working on kennel training and is not yet potty trained, so he’ll need a patient family ready to help him learn with consistency and positive reinforcement. If you’re looking for a playful buddy with plenty of cuddles to share, this handsome boy could be your perfect match!

Clay is small but mighty, and very feisty. She's started to come out of her shell more and more. She is good with other dogs, and cats, she just wants to play them. She is teething, and likes to chew and still figuring out what she can and cannot chew on. She is SUPER cuddly and playful. Clay is starting to figure out her voice, and loves to make noises. 214629314.description:
Hashbrown is a sweet, affectionate, high-energy pup with plenty of personality. Like most puppies, he’s curious, playful, and still learning the ropes—including his house manners! He isn’t housetrained yet and is definitely a little bitey, so having plenty of appropriate chew toys around is a must. He’s always ready for a good game or something fun to sink his teeth into.

Hashbrown loves to eat, explore, and get into a little mischief. He’s pretty good with kids and would love a family who can keep up with his puppy energy while helping him learn and grow.

When meeting other dogs, Hashbrown can be a little nervous at first, but his curiosity usually wins out. With patience and positive introductions, he’s learning how much fun canine friends can be.

If you’re looking for a playful, affectionate pup with a goofy streak and lots of potential, Hashbrown might just be your perfect match!
